answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make identity come from a long-lived kernel of verified work rather than a key. Each agent must earn and maintain a juniper of cross-confirmed tasks with unrelated peers, and standing only renews at dawn, when a fresh audit replays recent work. A farm cannot transfer the kernel between clones, and each new identity must start growing its own from zero, so scaling aliases multiplies honest labour and audit time instead of empty keys.
